name: CZECHIA

flag.title: Flag of Czechia
flag.note: White, red & blue with blue wedge at hoist

lead: Czechia is in the middle of Europe. Germany, Austria, Slovakia and Poland surround it, so it has no sea. Prague is one of Earth's best-kept old cities.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Pop. 1.4 m — city on the Vltava

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Gentle mountains ring the country. The west is Bohemia, with rolling hills. The east is Moravia, with flat plains, vineyards and folk festivals.
The Vltava River winds 430 km through Czechia, under Prague's famous bridges. Pine forests cover the Šumava mountains.
animals: The Eurasian lynx is a spotted wildcat as big as a labrador. Hunters wiped it out, but people brought it back in the 1980s. Around 60 now live in the Bohemian hills.
Red deer bellow in misty autumn valleys. The great bustard, Europe's heaviest flying bird, still strolls across Moravian fields.
culture: Czechs drink more beer per person than anyone on Earth, about 150 litres a year. Pilsen invented golden lager in 1842. The Pilsner Urquell brewery still makes it there.
Marionettes (string puppets) are an old Czech art. They perform whole operas. On Christmas Eve, families watch fairy-tale films together.
history: Bohemia was the heart of the Holy Roman Empire, a union of lands, under King Charles IV. He founded Central Europe's first university in 1348 and built Charles Bridge in 1357.

In 1968, Soviet tanks crushed the Prague Spring, a time of new freedoms. In 1989, students filled Wenceslas Square. After 43 days of peaceful protest, one-party communist rule ended without a shot. This was the Velvet Revolution.
wows: Czechia has over 2,000 castles and country palaces, more than almost any European country.
Prague Castle is the world's largest ancient castle site, at nearly 70,000 square metres.
Czech writer Karel Čapek invented the word 'robot' in his 1920 play R.U.R.
Czech scientist Otto Wichterle made the first soft contact lenses at home, on Christmas Day 1961.
Czechs have drunk the world's most beer per person every year since 1993.
Czech doctor Jan Jánský first fully sorted blood into A, B, AB and O groups in 1907.
Czechia has 16 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, packed into a country smaller than Austria.

myths.myth: Czech Republic and Czechoslovakia are the same
myths.fact: Czechoslovakia split peacefully on 1 January 1993, into Czechia and Slovakia.
Prague is farther west than Vienna. 'Eastern Europe' was a political label, not a map fact.
